rationale: oopack_v1p8 is a compact C++ benchmark dominated by a few hot numeric kernels (matrix, FFT, complex-arithmetic loops) with heavy arithmetic and small control-flow graphs, so low-cost arithmetic and structural transforms are preferred over aggressive runtime-heavy ones. SUB gets the highest enablement across security and diversity because instruction substitution obscures the dense arithmetic at near-zero runtime and size cost, which matters most in tight loops. FLA carries the highest security gain since flattening the kernels' loops hides their structure well, but its runtime/size weights are kept moderate because these kernels are timing-sensitive and flattening dispatch overhead compounds in inner loops. BCF is enabled at a moderate level to add opaque-predicate layering without letting its per-iteration branching bloat the hot paths. SPLIT is cheap and safe, so it is favored mainly for diversity, breaking up basic blocks to complement SUB and FLA. IBR and ICALL are enabled moderately: indirect branches and calls add resolution indirection that resists static call-graph recovery, with modest cost given the small number of calls in this benchmark. IGV is kept at moderate security/cost weights since the program has limited global state but OOP class tables and constants still benefit from hiding. CorrectnessRisk is kept low across the board (0.05-0.2) because C++ with virtual dispatch and exceptions tolerates these passes well, but FLA and IGV carry slightly higher risk weights to reflect their greater potential to perturb loop semantics and constant initialization.
